sections.label: Bill implements Committee recommendations
sections.summary: The Bill implements Committee recommendations, including decoupling admission from practice training contracts, lengthening training to one year, and limited practice rights.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The respondents comprised a good mix of practitioners, in-house counsel, law students, young lawyers and members of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This Bill contains amendments to implement these recommendations by the Committee: (a) decouple admission to the Singapore Bar from the completion of practice training contracts; (b) lengthen the practice training period from six months to one year; (c) confer on practice trainees limited rights to practise after six months of training; (d) permit up to three months of the practice training period to be completed at approved in-house legal departments of approved corporations; and (e) introduce a moratorium for practice training contract applications.

sections.label: Lawyer (NP) admission pathway
sections.summary: Part B passers can be admitted as lawyer (NP) without practice training, but need it to practise in law firms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Law graduates who pass the Part B examinations can now be admitted to the Singapore Bar as a lawyer (non-practitioner), or lawyer (NP), without needing to complete the prescribed practice training period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A lawyer (NP) does not have the right to practise in law firms and similar entities; instead a lawyer (NP) can adopt alternative pathways such as becoming in-house counsel or in academia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The prescribed practice training period remains compulsory for a lawyer (NP) who wishes to practise law in a law firm or similar entity.

sections.label: Lengthening practice training period
sections.summary: The Committee recommended lengthening the practice training period from a minimum of six months to one year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Moving on, I also wish to highlight that the Committee also recommended lengthening the practice training period, which is currently a minimum of six months, to one year.

sections.label: Provisional PC after six months
sections.summary: A lawyer (NP) who is a practice trainee may apply for a provisional PC after at least six months of practice training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A lawyer (NP) who is a practice trainee may apply for a provisional PC after completing at least six months of practice training.

sections.label: Provisional PC trainee work scope
sections.summary: A practice trainee with a provisional PC may do work a practising A&S may do, under supervising solicitor supervision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A practice trainee who has a provisional PC will be able to undertake work that a practising A&S may do – for example, appear and plead in Court, and render legal advice to clients – provided this is done under the supervision of his or her supervising solicitor.

sections.label: In-house practice training flexibility
sections.summary: The Bill lets practice trainees complete up to three months of training at approved in-house legal departments of approved non-law practice entities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The next amendment in the Bill provides flexibility for practice trainees to complete up to three months of their practice training at approved in-house legal departments of approved non-law practice entities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To ensure that these practice trainees receive proper supervision and training within the in-house legal department, an approved non-law practice entity must be of a minimum size and handle a reasonable amount of Singapore law-related work.

sections.label: Moratorium on practice training contracts
sections.summary: The Committee recommended a moratorium period before which law students cannot apply for practice training contracts and law practices cannot offer them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Committee recommended a moratorium period, before which law students cannot apply for practice training contracts and law practices cannot offer them.

sections.label: New admission framework effective date
sections.summary: The new admission framework will take effect from the 2024 session of the Part B Bar Examinations onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As announced by my Ministry earlier in February this year, the new admission framework will take effect from the 2024 session of the Part B Bar Examinations onwards.

sections.label: A&S admission under current framework
sections.summary: They can apply for admission as an A&S under the current framework if they pass the Part B examinations by a prescribed date in the second half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: They will be able to apply for admission as an A&S under the current admission framework if they pass the Part B examinations by a date prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This prescribed date will be in the second half of 2025.

sections.label: CPTL 2018 structural recommendations
sections.summary: The CPTL made three structural recommendations in 2018 which the Government accepted: lengthening practice training, raising Part B standards, and uncoupling admission from practice training contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When the rule of law suffers, the country suffers".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It was in that context, that the CPTL made three key structural recommendations in 2018 which the Government subsequently accepted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They are: (a) lengthening the practice training period from six months to a year; (b) raising the standard and stringency of the bar exams known as "Part B examinations"; and (c) uncoupling the admission to the Bar from the completion of practice training contracts.

sections.label: Trainee rotation to contrasting practice areas
sections.summary: In the new regime, each trainee would be required to rotate to contrasting practice areas to gain more exposure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the new regime, each trainee would be required to rotate to contrasting practice areas to gain more exposure.

sections.label: No charging for trainee work
sections.summary: Law practices currently are not allowed to charge clients for work done by their practice trainees under the supervision of their supervising solicitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the same time, law practices currently are not allowed to charge clients for the work done by their practice trainees, under the supervision of their supervising solicitors.

sections.label: Singapore bar exam pass rates
sections.summary: The CPTL report said Singapore's 2010-2016 bar exam pass rate of 99% compares favourably with England's and New York's rates of about 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In its report, the CPTL highlighted that the pass rate for the Singapore bar exams between 2010 to 2016, which stands at 99%, compares very favourably with the pass rates in the Bar exam in England, which is about 70%, and the New York Bar, which is about 70% too.

sections.label: Provisional practising certificate period doubled
sections.summary: The proposal would double the period during which practice trainees can practise with provisional practising certificates, differing from the current part-called lawyer regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A significant difference between the proposal and the current regime involving part-called lawyers is that the period during which practice trainees can practise, with provisional practising certificates is proposed to be doubled.

sections.label: JSO and LSO training periods
sections.summary: For JSOs and LSOs, six months of service equals one month of supervised private practice training, so three years typically equals six months of traineeship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For them, six months of working as a judicial service officer (JSO) or legal service officer (LSO) is equivalent to one month of supervised training by a practice trainee in private practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In other words, it typically takes three years for a JSO or LSO to complete the equivalent of six months' traineeship by a practice trainee, before he or she may be called to the Bar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If memory serves me correctly, I believe this requirement was first imposed in the early 1990s as part of a talent retention programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note from the CPTL report that it is proposed that the practice training period for law graduates who are serving as officers be equalised with practice trainees who serve their practice training period in Singapore law practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As a matter of principle, I support the parity, but may I please ask what is the Government's position on this matter, and if the Government accepts the CPTL's recommendation, may I ask how it proposes to deal with the original objective that led to the implementation of the different training periods for these officers in the first place?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments have the effect not only of changing certain aspects of new lawyers' training regime, but also restructures the legal profession by introducing a new category "lawyer (non-practitioner)", or lawyer (NP).

sections.label: In-house practice training contracts
sections.summary: The Ministry intends to allow, via subsidiary legislation, up to three months of a practice training contract to be completed at approved in-house legal departments of approved corporations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, I note that the Ministry intends to now allow, via subsidiary legislation, up to three months of a practice training contract to be completed at approved in-house legal departments of approved corporations.

sections.label: Law practice sizes and value added
sections.summary: A 2018 SingStat report found 97% of Singapore law practices have 30 or fewer practitioners, contributing 38% of value added, while the 3% larger firms contributed 62%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on a SingStat report in 2018, 97% of law practices in Singapore have 30 and less practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their value-added contribution, however, was only 38%, while the 3% of larger firms, contributed to 62% of value add.

sections.label: Practice training period lengthened
sections.summary: MinLaw announced when the amendment Bill was read for the first time that Legal Profession Act regulations would be amended to lengthen practice training from six months to one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: According to MinLaw's announcement made when the amendment Bill was read for the first time, the Legal Profession Act regulations would be amended to lengthen the practice training period from six months to one year.

sections.label: Practice training period financial hardship
sections.summary: Asks whether MinLaw considered that lengthening the practice training period by six months may cause financial hardship on law students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Has MinLaw considered the fact that lengthening the practice training period by a further six months may cause financial hardship on law students?

sections.label: New Bar admission category
sections.summary: Clause 6 of the Amendment Bill provides for a new category of individuals to be admitted to the Singapore Bar as a lawyer (NP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Amendment Bill provides for a new category of individuals to be admitted to the Singapore Bar as a lawyer (NP).

sections.label: Existing legal counsels Bar admission
sections.summary: Asks whether, if the law is passed, all existing legal counsels could apply to be admitted to the Bar as lawyers (NP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Further, if this law is passed, would all the existing legal counsels be able to apply to be admitted to the Bar as lawyers (NP)?

sections.label: Part B difficulty and lawyer shortage
sections.summary: Says MinLaw should accept a law graduate's academic knowledge, and making Part B harder adds stress amid a lawyer shortage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If a student has passed his or her examinations and graduated with a law degree, MinLaw should accept that that student does have the requisite academic legal knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Making Part B more difficult would merely add on the stress of being a lawyer when the legal profession is currently suffering from a shortage of lawyers.

sections.label: Extension of practice training period
sections.summary: Comments on the extension of the practice training period, saying increasing it from six to 12 months offers some advantages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My next comment, regarding the impact of these amendments on candidates seeking for admission relate to the extension of the practice training period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Increasing the training period from six to 12 months offers some advantages.

sections.label: Trainee costs and SkillsFuture subsidies
sections.summary: Raises trainee concerns over low pay extended to 12 months and no paid or sick leave, and asks about SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, it is essential to contemplate the consequences for both trainees and the law firm that engage them, particularly in terms of associated costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are two direct consequences that trainee remain concerned about: low pay is extended to 12 months instead of six months and no paid or sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Considering the financial constraints that may affect the decision to practise, is there possibility of utilising the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidies to financially support selected trainees during their practice training period?

sections.label: Trainees doing associate work
sections.summary: The proposal lets firms have trainees do associate work without paying them associate remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While enhancing a trainee's practical application of legal knowledge, this proposal also means that firms can now get trainees to do associate work without the trainee receiving the same renumeration as an associate.

sections.label: Longer training programme duration
sections.summary: Extending training from six to 12 months may give more assessment time and client continuity but may reduce contracts offered to trainees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While extending the training programme from six to 12 months may allow additional time for law firms to assess and evaluate trainees and may enable continuity of services for the firms' clients, the longer duration may result in a reduced number of contracts being offered or being available to trainees.

sections.label: Uncoupling bar admission from training
sections.summary: The amendment uncoupling bar admission from practice training offers graduates a choice but may reduce practising lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment that proposes uncoupling admission to the bar from the completion of practice training offers a choice to law graduates and may assist retaining them in the legal field.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, it may also inadvertently lead to a decline in the number of graduates becoming practising lawyers.

sections.label: Legal Profession Act amendment objective
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Legal Profession Act to strengthen lawyer training and equip graduates with relevant skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today seeks to amend the Legal Profession Act, with the key objective of strengthening the professional training regime for lawyers in Singapore and to better equip law graduates with the relevant skills and competencies to meet the demands of our changing economy.

sections.label: Trainee monthly allowances
sections.summary: Trainees are paid monthly allowances or honorariums of between S$1,000 and S$2,500 during the PTP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: From the postings online and from the trainees I spoke to, they are paid monthly allowances or honorariums of between S$1,000 or S$2,500 each month during the PTP.

sections.label: Paid sick leave for trainees
sections.summary: It is submitted that paid sick leave should accrue for trainees after three months of employment with a law firm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Given that there are some similarities between trainees and employees, it is humbly submitted that paid sick leave should similarly accrue for trainees after three months of employment with a law firm.

sections.label: Training and employment contract similarities
sections.summary: Training contracts share significant similarities with employment contracts, justifying basic benefits like paid sick leave for trainees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Leaving aside the practical concerns that I had highlighted, I noted that there are significant similarities between training contracts and employment contracts, which justify providing certain basic employment benefits, such as paid sick leave, to trainees, which employees under the Employment Act currently enjoy.

sections.label: Trainee equipment and remuneration
sections.summary: The trainee uses the firm's equipment and resources and is remunerated through regular allowance, not commissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, the trainee has access to and uses the firm's equipment and resources in the course of his or her work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Fourth, the trainee is remunerated through regular allowance, rather by means of commissions or otherwise.

sections.label: Training contracts as contracts of service
sections.summary: Training contracts should be classified as contracts of service, so trainees should receive basic benefits like paid sick leave and annual leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Lastly, if a "contract of service" as defined under the Employment Act also includes "an apprenticeship contract", a fortiori, a training contract offered to graduates should likewise be classified as a "contract of service" with attendant benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Given that there is some semblance between training contracts and employment contracts, it is humbly submitted that trainees should likewise be accorded basic employment benefits, such as paid sick leave and annual leave for a start, during the PTP, with other benefits to be considered at a later stage.

sections.label: Key practice training amendments
sections.summary: Amendments decouple bar admission from practice training, increase the training period, allow limited practice rights after six months, and introduce a moratorium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Key amendments introduced include decoupling admission to the Singapore bar from practice training, increasing the practice training period, allowing limited rights to practise after six months’ training and introducing a moratorium for practice training contract applications.

sections.label: Trainee salaries and practice period
sections.summary: Big Four trainees earn about $2,000 to $2,500 while first-year associates get $7,500 to $7,900, and a longer training period means lower salary for longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, it is reported that the Big Four law firms in Singapore pay trainees an honorarium of around $2,000 to $2,500 while their first-year associates now get $7,500 to $7,900.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The effect of increasing the practice training period to one year is that practice trainees will earn a lower salary for a longer period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share what steps will be taken across the board to review practice trainee salaries?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Singapore, one in seven junior lawyers stopped practising in 2021.

sections.label: Law graduates and practitioners numbers
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2021, Singapore averaged 394 law graduates yearly, and as of August 2023 the Law Society reports 6,512 practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2021, Singapore saw an average of 394 university graduates obtaining a first degree in law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of August 2023, the Law Society reports 6,512 practitioners.

sections.label: Practice training allowance quantum
sections.summary: Figures between $1,000 and $2,500 were shared as a rough quantum of allowance during practice training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Figures between $1,000 and $2,500 have been shared as a rough quantum of allowance during practice training.

sections.label: Trainee criteria and allowance guidelines
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether criteria exist to ensure trainees gain enriching experience comparable to peers in law firms, and what allowance guidelines apply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although this expands the opportunities for trainees and also provides a potential pipeline of support for these companies, I would like to ask if there are any criteria imposed to ensure that trainees can gain an enriching experience comparable to their peers who are practising with law firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What will the allowance guidelines be for trainees who choose to pursue this path?

sections.label: Circumstances warranting suitability examination
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry to describe circumstances warranting such an examination and how suitability to practise is determined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For greater clarity, could the Ministry describe what sort of circumstances will warrant such an examination and how will the Council or Attorney-General determine when one is not suitable to practise?

sections.label: Revision of modules and topics
sections.summary: The latest revision sees students completing six modules across a wide breadth of 31 topics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The latest revision sees students completing six modules across a wide breadth of 31 topics.

sections.label: Feedback on trainee training
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry has gathered feedback on the breadth and depth of training received by trainees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry gathered feedback on the breadth and depth of training received by trainees?

sections.label: Minimum wage for trainees
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Law Society will consider mandating a minimum wage for trainees similar to housemen's pay in medicine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, will the Law Society consider mandating a minimum wage for trainees similar to what housemen are paid in the medical field?

sections.label: Measures for young legal professionals
sections.summary: The passage asks what measures are being taken to rectify an issue and ensure a more sustainable and nurturing atmosphere for young legal professionals, citing a jailed, fined and disbarred lawyer who abused employees including a trainee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What measures are being taken to rectify this issue and ensure a more sustainable and nurturing atmosphere for young legal professionals?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask this because this House would recall that a lawyer of 20 years' standing was jailed, fined and disbarred for having abused his employees, among whom was a trainee.

sections.label: Longer practice period concerns
sections.summary: The passage states that the longer practice period aids career decisions but may exacerbate the existing shortage of legal professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It aids them in deciding their career goals and which specific areas to pursue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that the longer practice period, while beneficial in many aspects, may exacerbate the existing shortage of legal professionals.

sections.label: Legal Profession (Amendment) Bill speech
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker is a legislator speaking on the Legal Profession (Amendment) Bill, addressing practice opportunities for aspiring lawyers and balancing training time with the shortage of legal professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, in a strange twist of fate, I am now a legislator as a Member of Parliament, working alongside lawyers, legal professionals and Parliamentary Clerks, scrutinising Bills and legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I am speaking on the Legal Profession (Amendment) Bill because I believe this marks a substantial stride forward in advancing our legal field, particularly in addressing concerns over ample practice opportunities for aspiring lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While augmenting training time is beneficial, it is imperative to consider its potential impact on the shortage of legal professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Striking a balance between quality training and meeting the increasing demands of society is imperative to ensure a sustainable and thriving legal profession in Singapore.

sections.label: First batch practice training period
sections.summary: The passage states the first batch of law graduates under the new admission framework will commence their practice training period in January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The first batch of law graduates under the new admission framework will commence their practice training period, or PTP, in January 2025.

sections.label: Uncoupling admission from practice training
sections.summary: The passage states uncoupling admission from practice training will let those not intending to practise pursue other legal roles without completing the PTP and reduce competition for practice training positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Uncoupling admission from practice training will allow those who do not intend to practise to pursue other legal roles without investing additional time to complete the PTP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This will, in turn, reduce the competition for practice training positions.

sections.label: MinLaw amending subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: The passage states MinLaw is working with multiple stakeholders to amend subsidiary legislation to include further operational details before the new framework comes into force by July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MinLaw is working with the multiple stakeholders to amend the subsidiary legislation to include further operational details before the new framework comes into force by July 2024.

sections.label: Practice trainee honoraria and benefits
sections.summary: Practice trainees typically receive honoraria but not employee benefits such as paid leave or CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On this basis, practice trainees today typically receive honoraria, but do not receive employee benefits, like paid leave or Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions.

sections.label: MinLaw view on prescriptive measure
sections.summary: MinLaw has considered the measure but says it is prescriptive, introduces rigidity and would need constant review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: While MinLaw has considered this, such a measure is prescriptive, introduces rigidity and would need to be constantly reviewed to account for prevailing conditions.

sections.label: Leave days for practice trainees
sections.summary: MinLaw, SILE and the Law Society are looking into granting practice trainees leave days and medical leave under the lengthened PTP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MinLaw, SILE and the Law Society are already looking into granting practice trainees leave days and medical leave to support them through their PTP, as part of the overall implementation of the lengthened PTP.

sections.label: Twelve-month practice training period
sections.summary: Under the new framework, the PTP will be 12 months for all trainees across the industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Under the new framework, the PTP will be 12 months for all trainees across the industry.

sections.label: New Part B Course
sections.summary: The new Part B Course was introduced in the 2023 session.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The new Part B Course was introduced in the 2023 session.

sections.label: Qualifying entity criteria consultation
sections.summary: Further details on the application process and criteria for qualifying entities will be announced later, following a 2019 public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Further details, including the formal application process and finalised criteria for qualifying entities, will be announced in due course.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To provide insight, MinLaw had, in 2019, publicly consulted on the qualifying criteria proposed by the working group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: They included suggestions that the entity should: have a minimum of three lawyers doing legal work; have at least one Singapore-qualified lawyer with at least five years of legal experience, either in-house or in active practice, within the last seven years, who will act as supervising counsel to the trainee; and handle a sufficient amount of Singapore law-related work for the trainee to receive meaningful training in Singapore law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The majority of the respondents supported the criteria proposed in the public consultation.
